verdict.summary: LIN-GTB-2 was read faithfully: no missing content, no invented content, all quotes exact, DEC-0001..0007 recorded and sensible, Q-0001/Q-0002 well formed. Two Medium gaps for the synthesizer: the form-field limit (DEC-0003) and the server limit (DEC-0001) count characters differently and no criterion says what web/app do when orders-service rejects a note; FR-0001.AC-1's "alone or in the order list" lets the list omit the note that FR-0002/FR-0003 need. Two Low notes. No question filed, no commits. Globuli's generic checklist was not readable from this run.

findings.title: Field limit and server limit count differently; no criterion for a note orders-service rejects
findings.evidence: decisions.md DEC-0001: "counts Unicode characters (code points) of the note after trimming". DEC-0003: "accepts at most 280 characters" with no definition of a character. FR-0002.AC-3 and FR-0003.AC-3 only say the field holds the first 280 characters; neither requirement has a criterion for an HTTP 400 from FR-0001.AC-3. `node -e "[...'👨‍👩‍👧'].length"` prints 5.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer types 280 family emoji into the app's note field. Flutter's length limiter counts grapheme clusters, so the field accepts them; orders-service counts 1400 code points and answers HTTP 400 (FR-0001.AC-3). FR-0003 says nothing about what the app shows or whether the order is placed, so the coder and QA have no observable expectation.
findings.suggested_fix: In DEC-0003 define the field's count as DEC-0001's (code points after trimming), or state both ends count the same unit. Add a criterion to FR-0002 and FR-0003: when orders-service rejects the order because of the note, the form shows the error, keeps the customer's input and places no order. Say in DEC-0001 whether CRLF is normalised to one character.

findings.title: FR-0001.AC-1 'alone or in the order list' lets the list omit the note dependents need
findings.evidence: FR-0001.AC-1 Then: "fetching that order, alone or in the order list, returns the same note text". FR-0002.AC-4 needs a note icon per order in the web list; FR-0003.AC-4 needs the note's text per order in My orders.
findings.failure_scenario: The coder adds deliveryNote to the single-order response only; AC-1 passes on "alone". The web order list then has no way to know which orders have a note without fetching each one, and FR-0002.AC-4 cannot be built as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to "both when fetched alone and in the order list" and add an example row for the list response.

findings.title: Whether the note field is multi-line is unspecified in FR-0002 and FR-0003
findings.evidence: DEC-0002: "Line breaks inside the note are kept." Q-0002 asks whether a note may contain line breaks. FR-0002.AC-3 and FR-0003.AC-3 describe only the length limit. prd/modules/web.md and mobile.md list "None" under Open questions.
findings.failure_scenario: The web coder renders a single-line input; a customer cannot enter the line break that FR-0001's example row ("Ring twice" + line break + "Back door") and DEC-0002 allow, and QA has no criterion to say which is right.
findings.suggested_fix: State in FR-0002.AC-3/FR-0003.AC-3 whether the field is multi-line, and list Q-0002 under web.md and mobile.md open questions.

findings.title: Q-0001 and Q-0002 not linked from FR-0001's open_questions
findings.evidence: `open_questions: []     # Q-0001 and Q-0002 ask the client to confirm; they don't block`. The kb-critic constitution links a client question from the requirement's open_questions with blocks: [] in decide mode; prd/modules/orders.md lists both questions.
findings.failure_scenario: Whatever generates the visit agenda or traces a question to its requirement from open_questions misses FR-0001, so the client's answer to Q-0001 or Q-0002 is not applied to FR-0001. Medium confidence: if CI's Definition of Ready rejects a non-empty open_questions for a ready requirement, the synthesizer's choice is correct.
findings.suggested_fix: Set open_questions: [Q-0001, Q-0002] on FR-0001 if the Definition of Ready allows it; otherwise record why it doesn't.

outputs.description: Critic report: reading check, decisions, questions, findings
